activation_scope.eligible_tasks: only the fixed no-op task profile created by scripts/run_controlled_claude_worker_activation.py on the pinned canonical orchestrator-sync board, with a pre-acquired global one-shot lease, receipt-bound task/body/capsule digest, current dispatcher-owned binding, positive A3 gate, and claimed run
activation_scope.workspace: the claimed task's declared task-id workspace only

limits.budget_policy: use existing Claude subscription only; abort on rate-limit or provider error; no automatic retry

stop_switch.primary: latch native A3 revocation on the named task
stop_switch.effect: preparation and terminal interpretation refuse; the result cannot complete the task
stop_switch.secondary: reclaim is a bounded abort request: it fences the result immediately; the executor observes lost ownership on its next 20-second heartbeat and terminates its own registered Claude process group
stop_switch.replacement_rule: do not start a replacement worker until the aborted group exit is recorded
stop_switch.persistent_service_stop: not applicable: no daemon, cron, launchd, systemd unit, or warm pool is enabled

rollback: Do not invoke again after any failure, timeout, rate limit, fence loss, A3 revocation, parser error, or reviewer objection.
Record the native refusal or blocked state; reclaim only the named task if still running; wait for and record executor group exit before any replacement.
Remove only the task-owned temporary workspace after the task lifecycle is terminal and evidence is retained.
Leave broker wrapper disabled/shadow-only and do not alter provider credentials, config, routing, deployments, trading, or external messaging.
preconditions: All source and controlled-invocation harness hashes below match the worktree at invocation time.
Both retained disposable canary evidences have independent PASS review.
The live task is explicitly named in an invocation receipt before Claude starts.
The one-time bootstrap creates only the persisted Claude session binding; the one controlled worker execution is exactly one resume through the executor wrapper.
Both calls use provider-enforced plan mode, an explicit built-in tool denylist, safe mode, strict MCP configuration, and max-turns=1; no generic task can be invoked by this packet.
A durable global one-shot lease is acquired before task creation and pins the execution to the canonical orchestrator-sync board; any existing lease causes refusal.
The task's provider is claude-code and its mapping is dispatcher-owned, fresh, and unretired.
A positive A3 gate is present immediately before preparation and is not revoked at terminal handling.
No second controlled worker currently has an active claimed run.
excluded: deployments, merges, pushes, pull requests, or production runtime mutation
credentials, tokens, password access, or provider-account changes
cross-provider routing, automatic retries, or scheduler activation
next_gate: independent final activation-packet review, then one named controlled task only
